sections.narration: Could old armour stop a bullet? Sometimes. The answer depends on the armour and the weapon.
Mail armour uses linked rings. Steel plate armour can deflect some blows away from the body.
When firearms spread, steel armour was hardened, thickened, or given a reinforcing layer over the breastplate.
In proof tests, bullets hit some steel breastplates. A surviving dent showed that particular shot had stopped.
But one successful test was no universal guarantee. Armour and firearms evolved together for centuries; protection always had limits.
